prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: One historian of the city calls the column, over the fifty years it ran, the city's ______.

worlds.passage: From 1880 to 1930 the weekly paper of a small river city carried an unsigned column on its front page. The city had no railway until 1928, and the column's author read the foreign newspapers that reached the river port by steamer, weeks late. Each week he summarized wars, elections and inventions abroad, and diaries from the period show families learning of the telephone, the deaths of distant kings and the outbreak of war in Europe from his column before any other source. One historian of the city calls the column, over the fifty years it ran, the city's ______.
worlds.explanation: In a city cut off from the railway, the column carried news of the wider world in before anything else did, so it was the city's "portal." "Rudder" fails because the column reported on events abroad rather than steering the city's own decisions. "Ritual" fails because the column was read for its news, which changed every week. "Rampart" fails because the column let the outside world in rather than defending the city against it.

rudder.quote: summarized wars, elections and inventions abroad
rudder.why: its content concerned distant events, not the direction of the city's own affairs

ritual.why: readers came to it for new information, not for a repeated custom

rampart.why: the column made up for the city's isolation by bringing news in, the reverse of keeping something out

worlds.passage: From 1880 to 1930 the weekly paper of a small river city carried an unsigned column on its front page. In weeks when the city council had a vote coming, its author reviewed each measure and ended with one word, "yes" or "no"; in other weeks the column did not appear. Diaries from the period show councillors and their families reading the column before every vote, and of some six hundred measures in those years, among them the bridge, the waterworks and the new school, only a few dozen went against that word. One historian of the city calls the column, over the fifty years it ran, the city's ______.
worlds.explanation: Councillors waited for the column's verdict, and nearly every measure went the way it said, so the column was the city's "rudder," steering its course. "Portal" fails because the column dealt with the city's own business, not news from outside. "Ritual" fails because it appeared only when a vote was due and mattered for its verdicts. "Rampart" fails because the column directed the city's choices rather than defending it from an outside threat.

portal.why: the column dealt with local decisions, not with bringing in news of the wider world

ritual.quote: in other weeks the column did not appear
ritual.why: the column ran only when a vote was due, so it was no fixed, repeated observance

rampart.quote: the bridge, the waterworks and the new school
rampart.why: these are projects the city chose and built, not attacks it was protected against

worlds.passage: From 1880 to 1930 the weekly paper of a small river city carried an unsigned column on its front page. Every weekend after the midday meal, families across the city read it aloud, the eldest at the table reading and the others listening from fixed seats. Its contents changed little from week to week, mostly tide tables, church notices and the same few proverbs, and diaries from the period mention the weekend reading far more often than anything the column said. One historian of the city calls the column, over the fifty years it ran, the city's ______.
worlds.explanation: Families read the column aloud every weekend in a fixed way, even though it said almost the same thing each week, so it was the city's "ritual," valued for the practice rather than the content. "Portal" fails because the column brought in no news of the outside world. "Rudder" fails because it offered nothing that steered the city's decisions. "Rampart" fails because nothing threatened the city that the column defended against.

portal.quote: tide tables, church notices and the same few proverbs
portal.why: its contents were local and repetitive, with no news from beyond the city

rudder.quote: Its contents changed little from week to week
rudder.why: an unchanging column of notices and proverbs could not steer the city's decisions

rampart.quote: far more often than anything the column said
rampart.why: what mattered was the act of reading, not any stand the column took against a threat

worlds.passage: From 1880 to 1930 the weekly paper of a small river city carried an unsigned column on its front page. Three times the provincial government proposed merging the city into the larger town across the river. Weekly until the plan was dropped, the column listed the clauses of the city's 1790 charter that the merger would break, and the province's minutes cite those lists in withdrawing each plan. Diaries from the period show families untroubled by each plan, and the city kept its own council until 1931, a year after the column ended. One historian of the city calls the column, over the fifty years it ran, the city's ______.
worlds.explanation: Each time the province tried to absorb the city, the column's lists of broken charter clauses turned the plan back, families felt secure behind it, and the city lost its council only after the column ended, so the column was the city's "rampart." "Portal" fails because the column worked to keep an outside power out. "Ritual" fails because its campaigns answered specific threats. "Rudder" fails because the column acted against plans imposed from outside rather than guiding the city's own choices.

portal.quote: proposed merging the city into the larger town
portal.why: the column opposed an outside power coming in, the reverse of opening the city to the world

ritual.quote: cite those lists in withdrawing each plan
ritual.why: the column's campaigns answered specific threats and had concrete effects, not the empty repetition of a custom

rudder.quote: the province's minutes cite those lists
rudder.why: the column worked on the province's plans, repelling them, rather than setting the direction of the city's own affairs
